analysis:
Examined MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (base text lines 1-1013). Per file_changes, the PR moves the media-path reasoningPrefix computation (ReasoningPromptProbe.streamingPrefix ?? contentSeed) before bridge.submitTokenized, and passes a new stopStringScope (ReasoningStopScope.scope(reasoningParser:reasoningPrefix:)) to the bridge. Further hunks near head lines 975-976 and 1106-1108 are likely the same pattern on the text path, but they sit outside the supplied base text. Only the base side is visible and the patch excerpt is truncated, so head-side behavior could not be fully verified.

Security view: the change shapes stop-string matching against reasoning vs content state. It does not alter authorization, encryption, cache scope (requestCacheScope/cacheEnabled still passed unchanged, so T-041 scoping is preserved), release/reservation handling (releaseBox.fire and mediaGate.release paths in the catch block are unchanged), or the coordinator trust boundary. The new code runs after mediaGate.release and checkFirstContentDeadline, and inside the do/catch, so any throw from it still releases the lease and reservation. The call is non-throwing apart from tokenizer decode, which is pure.

Remaining questions for integration: (1) confirm ReasoningStopScope and the bridge's stopStringScope parameter cannot suppress or leak stop sequences in a way that bypasses max-token or stop enforcement, which is a correctness concern rather than a confidentiality one; (2) confirm the text path at head lines ~975 passes the same scope consistently; (3) the removed lines at base 750-761 were the old reasoningPrefix computation, so verify there is no duplicate or stale use after the move. No concrete security regression was identified in the visible evidence.
